root.name: Ruy Lopez: Old Steinitz Defense, Semi-Duras Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 d6 4. d4 Bd7 5. c4

overview: White takes space with c4 and d4 against Black's compact ...d6/...Bd7 set-up, so the Semi-Duras is a cramped but sound defence. Black usually plays ...Nf6, ...Be7 and ...exd4 at the right moment, while White presses with the centre pawns and Nc3.

white_ideas.idea: Keep e4, d4 and c4 pawns in the centre and squeeze Black
Develop Nc3, O-O, Re1 and force ...exd4 on White's terms

black_ideas.idea: Challenge the centre with ...exd4 when the timing is right

typical_structures.structure: Tense e4/e5 centre with Black's bishop on d7

character.notes: Slow manoeuvring game; Black is passive but hard to hurt.

soundness.notes: Old Steinitz is considered sound though passive.

structure.notes: c4/d4/e4 against d6/e5: centre in tension, usually resolved with ...exd4.

approach.notes: Standard Ruy Lopez sideline; not a system.

level.notes: Black must time the ...exd4 break; little forced theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Main line with exd4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black concedes the centre and White gets a Maroczy-style grip.

character.reason: Black's cramped, compact set-up is hard to break down and play is steady.

soundness.reason: The Old Steinitz is passive but accepted as sound.

structure.reason: The centre stays in tension until ...exd4, and the Semi-Duras c4 set-up is undecided.

approach.reason: A Ruy Lopez sideline that stronger players use now and then, not a system.

level.reason: Plans are clear for White but Black must time ...exd4 correctly.

plans.reason: White's c4/d4/e4 pawns take space against the cramped Black position.
